title: Bi-Objective Contract Allocation for Guaranteed Delivery Advertising

problem.claim: Guaranteed Delivery advertising requires contract allocation that maximizes impressions assigned to new incoming orders while controlling inventory balance.

gap.claim: Existing work usually treats offline contract allocation and online impression serving separately, without accounting for practical online-serving situations during offline formulation.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates a bi-objective contract allocation problem for Guaranteed Delivery advertising.
The paper designs an efficient local search that alternates its focus between the two objectives for a high-dimensional, heavily constrained problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their algorithm outperforms multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and Gurobi.

narrative_sequence.summary: Guaranteed Delivery advertising systems contain offline selling and online serving stages.
Existing approaches generally handle the two stages separately and may formulate contracts without considering online-serving conditions.
The paper introduces bi-objective contract allocation and an alternating-objective local search for the constrained problem.
The authors report better performance than multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and Gurobi.
